content: xterm.js scrollback memory is non-trivial: a single 160x24 terminal with 5000 lines of scrollback uses ~34MB; multiplying by N persistent terminal instances scales linearly and each xterm.js instance also owns its own DOM canvas/webgl renderer, so many simultaneous live terminals cause real memory and render-perf pressure. Mitigation used by VS Code and others: cap scrollback per session, virtualize/detach DOM for non-visible terminals, keep only the active terminal's renderer live.
